mainEntity.name: What is risk of ruin in trading?

acceptedAnswer.text: Risk of ruin is the probability that a run of losses shrinks your account to the point you cannot keep trading it. The classical formula needs three inputs: win rate (p), payoff ratio (b = average win ÷ average loss), and risk per trade. Edge per trade is E = p·b − (1−p). If E is zero or negative, eventual ruin is 100% — no position size can fix a missing edge. If E is positive, ruin probability is ((1−E)/(1+E))^N, where N is your account divided by risk per trade — the number of risk units you hold.

mainEntity.name: What is a good risk of ruin percentage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most professional risk frameworks target a ruin probability of 1% or less. That is why this calculator's solver finds the maximum risk per trade that holds ruin under 1% — for the default 45% win rate at 1.5:1 payoff, that ceiling is about 5.5% per trade. Treat the solver's number as a ceiling, not a target: brokerage, STT and slippage are not in the model, so reality is always harsher than the formula.

mainEntity.name: How much should I risk per trade to avoid ruin?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no universal number — it depends on your edge — but 1% per trade is the robust starting point for most retail strategies. Take a 40% win rate with a 2:1 payoff (edge +0.2R per trade): at 1% risk the classical ruin probability is effectively 0%, but the identical strategy at 10% risk carries about 1.7% ruin. The ruin curve on this page makes the trade-off visible: drag the risk slider and watch ruin stay flat, then explode.

mainEntity.name: Does win rate or position size matter more for survival?

acceptedAnswer.text: Once you have an edge, position size dominates. Compare two strategies with the identical edge of +0.2R per trade — a 60% win rate at 1:1 payoff, and a 40% win rate at 2:1. At 10% risk per trade, both carry the same 1.7% ruin probability: the higher win rate bought no extra safety. But take either strategy from 1% risk to 10% risk and ruin goes from effectively zero to 1.7%. Edge decides whether you can survive; size decides whether you will.

mainEntity.name: Can a profitable strategy still blow up?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — positive expectancy plus oversized bets is the classic blow-up recipe. A 50% win rate at 1.5:1 payoff has a healthy edge of +0.25R per trade, yet at 25% risk per trade its classical ruin probability is about 13%. The strategy was profitable on paper and the account still died, because a normal losing streak at that size is an account-ending event. This is why the calculator pairs every ruin number with a maximum safe size.
